page: Amazon Web Services m4.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at 2.4 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32.0 GB of memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, and a 45 MB L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU bundled with this instance, and the baseline network bandwidth is 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the m4.2xlarge exhibits moderate multi-core and memory performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU score fall into the average category, as do the memory bandwidth metrics for both small and large blocks. However, single-core benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, are positioned in the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are categorized as weak. Large-model LLM text generation is poor, though text generation with a small 135M model achieves average tier speeds.

The instance offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, making it qualitatively cost-effective for legacy general-purpose workloads that require stable, dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high single-thread performance or local NVMe storage. The absence of local storage means all storage must be network-attached, which, combined with the 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, limits its suitability for high-throughput database or storage-heavy applications. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, multi-threaded background processing, and moderate memory-bound applications that can tolerate lower single-core execution speeds.
